w: In Dholka Swamishri performed the pratishtha rituals of the canvas murtis for the hari mandir in Bhoyka
At 5.25 p.m., Swamishri performed arti of Thakorji at the hari mandir in Purushottampura, where an annakut of vegetables (shak ni hatdi) was arranged.

At 10.25 am Swamishri arrived on the festival stage to give diksha to sadhaks and parshads into the parshad and bhagvati fold respectively. Swamishri gave the guru mantra and the senior sadhus gave kanthi, upper cloth and pagh to the newly initiated. The occasion became sublime with the singing of “Halo Juvanada Harivar Varva Helo Padyo’. Swamishri finally blessed the assembly, “To renounce home is very difficult. But due to the glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj the youths have taken diksha to worship God. It is indeed a great thing. Appreciations to their parents for giving their educated boys for diksha. The youths will inspire satsang in hundreds of thousands of people.” As part of the murti-pratishtha ceremony of the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and guru parampara a yagna was initiated. The yagna fire was lit with the flame brought from Chhapaiya and Chansad. Swamishri offered rice grains and ghee into the yagna kund. Thereafter Swamishri blessed the gathering.

Guest Opinion : Shri Raghunathan, Chief Secretary of Delhi State, stated, “I am totally humbled by what I saw. When I see every part of this Dham, each part is telling me about what a tradition we have imbibed, that we have inherited, and how precious this tradition is to us.”

Smt. Sheela Dixit, Chief Minister of Delhi, voiced, “It is something extraordinary. I have never experienced anything like this. I am still trying to recover from the impact it has left. It is really marvellous. Not only is it an extraordinary marvel of architecture, but there is spirituality, devotion, and faith that comes out of a visit to this structure.”

Shri Bawa Jain, Secretary General of the World Council of Religious Leaders, reflected, “I don’t think words can describe this experience. One really has to come here because whatever you see in photographs is just not enough for the vibration that you feel. If everybody can have this experience, I am sure and absolutely convinced there can be a deep transformation. This moves you to the core.”

Sam Cardon, World renowned Music Composer, Music Director of Neelkanth Yatra, was overwhelmed and said, “I have seen extraordinary sites, ancient temples – but something on this scale with architecture that is thousands of years old, in today’s world is just extraordinary. I can’t imagine anything that is its equal. And the fact that it’s been achieved by people who are devoted, and, I think, extraordinarily creative and organized – I mean just the logistical part of it – it just seems like an impossibility. And yet, it has been done with such a great spirit of cooperation. I just think it is an extraordinary achievement. I really applaud what has been done here.”

st.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj – Satsang Shikshan Pariksha Din – Saturday 4th November 2006
w: The evening assembly of Saturday 4 November 2006 saw the performance of a drama entitled ‘Karo Kankunã’ in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The drama provided glimpses into a family’s reluctance to take Satsang Exams and how through constructive use of time, one can find time to read and learn from Satsang books. Swamishri’s blessings were based on the drama: ‘To become happy in this world, we should look at others less fortunate than ourselves and realise how fortunate we are.’ At the end of his blessings, Swamishri asked everyone gathered to all pledge to take the Satsang Exams.

Swamishri was retiring to bed at night. Sadhus and devotees were engaged in Swamishri’s darshan. At that time Bhimo, one of the mandir cooks, was also doing darshan. Swamishri saw him and enquired as to when he had started wearing spectacles. Bhimo was called nearer, and Swamishri asked several questions regarding how he managed his life and expenses. Bhimo has been offering his services as a cook in the Sanstha for many years. Swamishri took interest and care in Bhimo and blessed him for his sincere services.

200 male and female devotees pilgrimaged 100 km by foot from Amreli, Dhari, Chalala and Devrajiya; 8 female and 13 male devotees from Derdi – Kumbhaji; 8 women and 3 male devotees from Mehta Khambhaliya; and 43 women and 15 male devotees from Moviya.

Pravinbhai Sheth of Kolkata came for darshan. As soon as he saw him, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "I have been remembering you for two days. Yesterday too I told the sadhus that for two days I have been seeing you from afar in the courtyard, so call him."

Seeing such affection from Swamishri, Pravinbhai was choked with emotion. Yesterday Swamishri had especially told the sadhus, "Do not forget those who are old and foundation devotees; remember them all and call them."

Pravinbhai Sheth of Kolkata came for darshan. As soon as he saw him, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "I have been remembering you for two days. Yesterday too I told the sants that for two days I have been seeing you from afar in the courtyard, so call him over."

Seeing such affection from Swamishri, Pravinbhai was choked with emotion. Yesterday Swamishri had specially told the sants, "Do not forget those who are old and who are founding devotees. Remember them all and call them over."

ds.t: First the methi, then the magas
w: Mahant Swami Maharaj began his breakfast. From his thal he gave Kothari Swami a piece of methi (fenugreek sweet) and also some magas, and said, "Eat the methi first, then the magas."

Everyone knows that "if one eats magas after methi, the bitterness goes from the mouth." Yet Swamishri cannot stop himself from giving even such ordinary suggestions, because he loves the devotees like a mother.

ds.t: What are the devotees eating today?
w: While eating, Mahant Swami Maharaj asked, "What is there for the devotees to eat today?"
Atmaswarupdas Swami said, "Sata, jalebi, undhiyu and rotli, made in their own homes and sent by devotees from the surrounding villages."
Swamishri was satisfied.
When sadhus have been arranging meals for devotees very responsibly for years, an ordinary person would never think of asking such a question. Swamishri does, because he truly cares for the devotees.
